look_here_first: Find ONE entire leaf: S. pilosior has only ONE PAIR of comparatively broad hairy leaflets, approximately 1.3–1.8 times as long as wide. Check for short retrorse hairs and much stiffer long setae on stems, the gland where both leaflets meet, then anthers and hairy upright fruit. Do not separate by annual versus perennial habit: current sources disagree on its life history.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: source conflict: Kew reports annual; 2024 taxonomic treatment reports herbaceous perennial — do NOT use life history for identification

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: exactly one leaflet pair per compound leaf

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaflets relatively broad, about 1.3–1.8 times as long as wide

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mixture of short retrorse hairs, glandlike trichomes and longer stiff setae on stems

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: extrafloral gland at the point where the paired leaflets join

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: persistent sepals on developing fruit; anthers constricted below symmetric terminal pollen pore

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: erect oblong pods roughly 2–4 cm long, hairy/setose; can persist after opening

lookalikes.differences: S. roemeriana also has one leaflet pair, but its leaflets are much more narrowly lanceolate (approximately 2–9 times as long as wide). S. bauhinioides also has a single broad pair; distinguish with stiff mixed stem hairs, persistent sepals, anther/pod detail, and S. bauhinioides stout thickened style + rough seed testa. Life history, leaflet count alone and yellow flowers do not separate this trio.
